plan.name: Tell agents that write files to write as they go
plan.summary: At max effort (D-0114), #91's build agent spent whole replies thinking and lost each one at the output limit before it wrote a file, so every prompt for an agent that writes files will say how its replies work: synthesis in each language and for existing code, formalization, and a plumbing issue's plan and build. One new function, synth.WriteAsYouGo in internal/synth/prompt.go, writes the paragraph for all of them, given the order to write files in, if any, and what the agent's budget is called: "A reply holds about 128,000 tokens of output, thinking included, and anything past that is cut off and lost: a reply that runs out of room loses what it didn't write. So write each file as soon as you've decided what it holds (<order>), rather than reasoning the whole job through in one reply. Writing files early costs none of your <budget>: they're for checking what you've written." Synthesis's order is the model first, then the code, then its contracts, then the explorer or driver, as its language has them (for existing code, the driver, then any change the model needs), formalization's is the module, then proposal.json, and a plan and a build name none; the budgets are gate runs, checks, checks and test runs. Max effort, each prompt's sentence stating its budget, and the reviewers' prompts, whose agents only read, stay as they are. This changes the trusted base, so a person merges it.

tests.name: TestSynthesisTellsTheAgentToWriteAsItGoes
tests.says: In Go, TypeScript and Python, and for existing code, the synthesis prompt says a reply holds about 128,000 tokens of output, thinking included, and one that runs out of room loses what it didn't write, so the agent writes each file as soon as it's decided, the model first for new code, which costs none of the gate runs the prompt still gives it.

tests.says: A plumbing build's prompt says a reply holds about 128,000 tokens of output, thinking included, and one that runs out of room loses what it didn't write, so the agent writes each file as soon as it's decided, which costs none of the test runs the prompt still gives it, and the reviewer's prompt, whose agent writes no file, doesn't tell it to.
